data.turoyo: Madamki hawxa yo, i aṯto kofərḏ̣o lu gawro qamoyo.
data.translation: Wenn das so ist, so gehört die Frau von Rechtswegen dem ersten Mann.

rationale: Better standalone context for a thin cell: explicit female subject and l-marked entitled person. 60/127 is already a parallel reference, but this ruling’s actual text is not quoted.

summary: All five occurrences support I.1 von Rechtswegen gehören. The female subject controls -o; l- marks the legally entitled person, including eli, elux and lu gawro qamoyo. These are not transitive imposed-duty constructions merely because the Arabic etymology includes that meaning.

The first two verses each contain two alternative predicates, and 60/127 states the ruling. Count five occurrence decisions, not five independent examples. One additional full ruling is enough; retain all inherited references and wording.
g-, gəd-, k- and ko- occur with the same Infectum predicate. They do not license a ko-Preterit box, since there is no Preterit base with an agent-series suffix here.
